title: A reproducible safety assessment model for concurrent transcranial magnetic stimulation with implanted intracranial electroencephalography electrodes
title_zh: 用于植入式颅内脑电电极的并发经颅磁刺激安全评估模型的可重复性研究
abstract: BACKGROUND: Concurrent transcranial magnetic stimulation and intracranial EEG (TMS-sEEG) offers a powerful approach for interrogating human brain circuits with high spatiotemporal resolution. However, standardized safety testing procedures for TMS in the presence of implanted electrodes are lacking. OBJECTIVE: To establish and validate a reproducible methodological framework for assessing TMS safety with sEEG hardware, addressing potential risks of electrode displacement, heating, and secondary current induction. METHODS: A conductive agarose phantom implanted with clinical-grade platinum sEEG electrodes was exposed to single-pulse TMS (0.4 Hz), repetitive TMS (1-50 Hz), and intermittent theta burst stimulation. Electrode displacement was quantified via high-speed video and motion tracking. Temperature changes were measured with fiber-optic thermal probes positioned at stimulated electrode contacts. Induced voltages were recorded using an oscilloscope and intracranial EEG hardware, and secondary current and charge density were calculated from oscilloscope outputs and impedance measurements. RESULTS: sEEG lead displacement remained micrometer-scale across stimulation conditions, with a maximum transient displacement of 10.99 μm and a maximum 1-s mean displacement from the pre-TMS position of 16.27 μm. Temperature changes remained well within the 2°C safety threshold across all tested conditions; in the primary temperature series, the maximum observed increase was 0.073°C. Induced voltages and charge densities remained below established safety limits, exhibiting consistent exponential decay with increasing distance from the coil. All stimulation conditions, including those exceeding typical clinical ranges, remained well within safety margins. CONCLUSIONS: Under the tested conditions in a controlled phantom environment, TMS exposure produced micrometer-scale transient and longer-timescale displacement, temperature changes within established safety thresholds, and charge densities within established safety thresholds. This validated methodological pipeline provides a standardized framework for future safety experiments involving TMS and implanted devices and supports continued development of TMS-sEEG as a tool for studying human brain circuitry and neuromodulation.
abstract_zh: 背景：并发经颅磁刺激（TMS）与颅内脑电（sEEG）相结合（TMS‑sEEG）为以高时空分辨率探测人脑电路提供了强大手段。然而，针对植入电极环境下的TMS标准化安全测试程序尚缺。目的：建立并验证一种可重复的方法框架，用于评估TMS与sEEG硬件的安全性，重点关注电极位移、加热和二次电流诱导等潜在风险。方法：在导电琼脂水凝胶模型中植入临床级钯sEEG电极，分别施加单脉冲TMS（0.4 Hz）、重复性TMS（1–50 Hz）和间歇性θ波束刺激。通过高速摄像和运动跟踪量化电极位移；使用光纤热探头测量刺激电极接触点的温度变化；利用示波器和颅内脑电硬件记录诱导电压，并根据示波器输出和阻抗测量计算二次电流和电荷密度。结果：在所有刺激条件下，sEEG导线位移保持在微米级，最大瞬时位移为10.99 µm，最大1 s平均位移为16.27 µm。温度变化始终低于2 °C的安全阈值；在主要温度序列中，最大升温仅为0.073 °C。诱导电压和电荷密度均低于既定安全限值，并随与线圈距离的增加呈指数衰减。所有刺激条件，包括超出典型临床范围的情况，均保持在安全边际内。结论：在受控模型环境下的测试条件中，TMS暴露产生了微米级的瞬时和长期位移，温度变化在既定安全阈值内，电荷密度亦在安全限值内。该验证的方法流程为未来涉及TMS与植入设备的安全实验提供了标准化框架，并支持TMS‑sEEG作为研究人脑电路和神经调控工具的持续发展。
